title: Audit whether go test caching is sound here, then decide about -count=1
description:
The gate passes -count=1, which disables Go's test cache entirely, so every package is re-run for every tick even when nothing it depends on changed.

Whether that can safely be dropped is NOT obvious, and three experiments on this machine disagreed:
- a package whose test reads a file INSIDE the package directory: cached, and correctly invalidated when the file changed.
- a package whose test reads a file ABOVE its own directory by a relative path: go refused to cache it at all (safe, just never fast).
- a test reading an ABSOLUTE path outside the module: cached, and NOT invalidated when the file changed. Unsound.
- and internal/sandboxpin, which reads the repo tree through contracts.RepoRoot(), caches cleanly in practice.

contracts.RepoRoot() builds from os.Getwd(), so it yields absolute paths - the shape that behaved unsoundly. The concrete risk is the drift guards: TestThisRepositorysGateIsReadable, the Makefile-matches-the-declared-gate test and the harness-bound-outlives-the-declared-bound test all read .tick/runners.toml. A cached pass surviving an edit to that file would leave those guards silently not guarding.

So this tick is an AUDIT first and a flag change second. If caching cannot be made sound for the guard tests, the answer may be to keep -count=1 for them and allow caching elsewhere, or to have those guards read their inputs in a way go tracks.

2026-10-07 21:21 - AUDIT ANSWERED (2026-10-07, attempt 9), demonstrated either way on this machine's go 1.26.2, not asserted.

(1) .tick/runners.toml, the Makefile, and every other in-module file a drift guard reads in-process: a cached pass CANNOT hide a change. cmd/go keys a package's cached result on the size+mtime of every in-module file the test binary opened (computeTestInputsID), so an edit invalidates. Pinned hermetically (TestACachedPassCannotHideAnEditToAFileAGuardReads, tick 6wh) and demonstrated on the real guards at the gate's own granularity: warm `make gate` (42 packages answered from cache), deliberate runners.toml drift (the go gate's -timeout 45m edited to 44m), third gate re-ran internal/reconcile UNCACHED (81s) and TestTheGateTargetMatchesTheDeclaredGate FAILED naming the drift while the other 42 packages stayed cached. Caching stays adopted; the flag stays as set 2026-09-18; runners.toml and the Makefile recipe unchanged.

(2) Two shapes CAN hide a change; both demonstrated and pinned as tests in internal/reconcile/gate_cache_soundness_test.go:
  - Subprocess reads are INVISIBLE to the cache (bash's opens never enter the test binary's input log). Demonstrated end-to-end at this tick's base commit: internal/ciwatchdog, warm, answered `ok (cached)` over a main-ci-watchdog.sh reduced to `exit 1`; -count=1 alone revealed every watchdog test failing. Three gate-visible guards had this shape — ciwatchdog's watchdog script, factory's wrangler-docker.sh, release's install.sh (the gate's one load-bearing test) — FIXED in this tick: each reads its script in-process before shelling out, so an edit invalidates the package and the guard re-runs the new script. Re-demonstrated at head: the same broken script re-runs and FAILS.
  - Files OUTSIDE the module are NEVER rechecked — deliberate in cmd/go ("Do not recheck files outside the module, GOPATH, or GOROOT root"), absolute or relative, read in-process or not. Demonstrated: a guard-shaped test reading an outside-module input was served `ok (cached)` after the input changed; -count=1 failed. No gate-visible guard reads repository drift from outside the module. The one outside-module guard by nature — wirevocab diffing the pinned herd vocabulary against the installed herdr — CANNOT be fixed by reading in-process; filed as a finding (medium) for the -count=1-for-that-package decision, which is a person's, not a worker's.

(3) Correction to this record's second experiment: a relative path above the package directory does NOT make go refuse to cache — the relative-outside read is cached and never invalidated, same as the absolute one (demonstrated). The refusal 6wh measured was cmd/go's fresh-mtime rule: an input written <2s before the run refuses caching.

(4) One uncached full run remains in the epic's lifecycle, unchanged: `make suite` (the paranoid answer), CI's race job (-count=1), and CI's full `make test` on ephemeral runners with no cache to consult.

acceptance_criteria: A written answer, on this tick, to whether a cached pass can ever hide a change to .tick/runners.toml or another input a guard test reads - demonstrated either way, not asserted. If caching is adopted, a deliberately edited runners.toml still fails the drift guards. One uncached full run remains somewhere in the epic's lifecycle.
